solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Despot's grilling poor, newspaper's admitted

indicators.note: to be admitted is to be let inside, so the newspaper word goes inside the other letters
grilling is a rough interrogation, so the next word is roughed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A tyrant's harsh interrogation of the poor is admitted by a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despot's' is the definition plus 'is'; 'grilling' looks like the tyrant's action but only signals the shuffle, and the newspaper word lands in the middle of the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor is one who rules harshly and unjustly, which is what a despot does.

clue.text: Old illuminators used small point for the most part

indicators.note: only the greater part of the word point is wanted, so its tail is cut away
something used has been handled and messed about, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: point with its last two letters removed

explanation.surface: Antique lamps once made use of a tiny point, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: Only three of the five letters of 'point' are kept, which is generous of 'for the most part'; the blog for this puzzle made the same objection.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps burning oil were the usual household lighting before gas and electricity, so they are illuminators of the past.

clue.text: No Conservative complaints about this philosophy

indicators.note: about suggests being turned around and moved here and there, so the letters are rearranged
No here means without, so the Conservative letter is dropped from the complaints

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political party with no complaints about a certain way of thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonism is the body of philosophy derived from Plato, so it is one particular philosophy.

clue.text: Demand former partner's given decree

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
an act is a decree passed into law

explanation.surface: An ex insists on something once granted a divorce decree.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain payment or compliance, as in exacting a toll.

clue.text: Insubstantial commercial set in flashy surroundings

indicators.note: set in places one thing inside another, here inside the word for flashy
surroundings are what lies all round, confirming that the flashy word encloses the other

explanation.surface: A flimsy advert placed among glitzy surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shadowy is faint and lacking substance, like a shadow itself.

clue.text: Check up after game with Norway becomes more fluid …

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the word for check runs backwards

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A check after a game against Norway makes something flow more freely.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next two in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Runnier is the comparative of runny, liquid enough to flow easily, so more fluid.

clue.text: Decoration's advancing with no hint of inharmoniousness

indicators.note: with no tells us the following letter is to be left out
a hint is just the first letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A medal is being awarded, with no hint of discord.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or honour; a gong also sounds, which suits the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a gong is a medal or honour, which is a decoration.

clue.text: .. obvious in extra time …

parts.note: an over is an extra amount, something left over
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something was plain to see when the game went into extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses chain this clue to its neighbours only in the surface reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly shown and not concealed, which is obvious.

clue.text: …sign of stratagem in internationals?

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the answer is a part of the following words

parts.note: the end of stratagem, then in, then the first letter of internationals

explanation.surface: A signal of tactics used in international matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: In Quebec French girl's scoffing bit of Norfolk dumpling

indicators.note: scoffing means eating, taking something inside, so the county letter goes in

parts.note: Que. is the official abbreviation for Quebec

indicators.note: bit of means only a small piece, the opening letter, of the county name

explanation.surface: In Quebec, a French girl munches a piece of an English county's dumpling.
explanation.walkthrough: The county letter is swallowed by the Quebec-plus-girl pair as a whole, at their join, rather than by the girl alone. Norfolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A quenelle is a small poached dumpling of fish or meat in French cooking.

clue.text: Cloth — some buckram — allocated for backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the found letters are read from right to left
some means only part of the following words is wanted

parts.note: the end of buckram and the start of allocated

explanation.surface: Some of the stiff buckram fabric has been set aside to back something.
explanation.definitionFit: Llama is also a fabric woven from the wool of the llama, so it names a cloth.

clue.text: Notice not applicable — employ a maiden for ever

parts.note: N/A is the abbreviation for not applicable
M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A job notice says it does not apply: hire a young woman permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for 'to the point of sickness', said of something going on endlessly.

clue.text: Trunk road circling castle (or island, with greater reason)

indicators.note: circling means going all the way round, so the road surrounds what follows

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest trunk road, written AI
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A main road runs around a castle or an island, the bracket adding an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is Latin for 'from the stronger', used to say a conclusion holds all the more strongly.

clue.text: Unacceptable, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: this says the word reads the same from either end, forwards or backwards

parts.note: the idiom for something that cannot be allowed, which is then checked against its own reversal

explanation.surface: Something is out of the question from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is a British idiom meaning not acceptable, as in 'that's just not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not on is a British idiom for its being unacceptable or out of order.

clue.text: Cardinal's prudish, fairly oddly

indicators.note: oddly here means taking letters in an irregular, every-other pattern rather than the whole word

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of fairly

explanation.surface: A cardinal of the church is rather strait-laced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' usually means the odd-numbered letters, which would give FIL; here the even ones are needed, so read it loosely as 'alternately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means chief or fundamental, as does primary.

clue.text: Quixote — unusual man — sadly sacking you and me one day in September?

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the remaining letters fall into a different order
sacking means dismissing, so the letters for you and me are thrown out

parts.note: you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Don Quixote, a strange man, sadly dismisses the pair of us one autumn day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' reads like an anagram signal but is part of the fodder; one U and the S are removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumnal equinox, when day and night are equal, falls around 22 or 23 September in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Fossil obscured by rare lichen

indicators.note: obscured by means concealed within the following words

parts.note: the end of rare and the start of lichen

explanation.surface: A fossil has been covered over by an uncommon lichen.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, and a fossil is a relic of ancient life.

clue.text: Designer of short evening dress featuring in guide

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing inside, so the dress goes within the guide

parts.note: a courier is a tour guide

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tux is a dinner jacket, formal evening dress

explanation.surface: A fashion designer of a short evening gown appears in a style guide.
explanation.walkthrough: A courier in British usage is a guide employed to look after a group of tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier is a designer who makes fashionable clothes, especially haute couture.

clue.text: How a lord might carry on with endless vendetta?

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to carry on with someone is to dally, flirt

explanation.surface: A nobleman might go on with a never-ending feud.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening words, an adverb completed by 'carry on', which also gives the wordplay; the setter confirmed this parse on the blog.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval lord ruled his vassals under the feudal system, so he behaved feudally.

clue.text: Medic rebuffing suitable design

parts.note: an MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: a rebuff turns something back, so the word for suitable is read backwards

explanation.surface: A doctor rejects a fitting plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a decorative design or pattern, especially a repeated one.

clue.text: Play fat cissy mostly on the right wing

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word before it
play means to mess about, so the letters are juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: A plump weakling is playing on the right wing in a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right wing' reads as a team position but defines a political stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Fascism lies at the far right of politics, so a fascist is on the right wing.

clue.text: Realise river's attractive

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Seeing that a river is pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' or 'has', joining the river to the adjective; 'Realise' looks like 'notice' but means carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a plan is to carry it out, which is to execute it.

clue.text: See 15
Lawyer's cloak material

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US
to cloak is to mask, disguise

explanation.surface: The cloth a lawyer's cloak is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric, often silk or linen, so a material.

clue.text: Try to shake off lumbago — trouble with disc?

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the remaining letters are disturbed into a new order
to shake off is to get rid of, so the word for try leaves the ailment

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: An attempt to cure back pain when the real problem is a slipped disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc' suggests the spine, after lumbago; it means a record.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record, a disc of music.

clue.text: Breathed a sound, getting more despondent

indicators.note: a sound is what is heard, so the spoken words stand for a different spelling

explanation.surface: Someone gave a sigh and felt lower and lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or low, so bluer means more despondent.

clue.text: Questionable political capital made from rich receiving entertainment in South Dakota

indicators.note: in means placed inside the abbreviation of the state that follows

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the entertainment word follows on directly

explanation.surface: Dubious party money comes from a wealthy donor entertained in South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: A slush fund is money set aside for illicit purposes such as bribery, especially in politics.

clue.text: Axed, ambassador took the plunge

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
to take the plunge is to get married

explanation.surface: An ambassador sacked from the job then got married.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewed is the past tense of hew, to chop with an axe.

clue.text: Performance by a Latin duo gets pats on the back

indicators.note: a performance puts things on show in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Latin American pair's show earns warm praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulation is lavish praise, figuratively a lot of pats on the back.

clue.text: Do the twist with Shirley? Pirouetting sure to be de trop

indicators.note: a pirouette is a spin, so the letters of the word for sure turn into another order
de trop means unwanted, too much, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Dancing the twist with Shirley, spinning around seems too much.
explanation.walkthrough: SEY is removed from the girl's name, its S from the front and EY from the end. De trop is French for superfluous.
explanation.definitionFit: To whirl is to spin round fast, which is what doing the twist describes.

clue.text: Sounding a bit on the borderline

indicators.note: sounding means as heard, so the spoken word is spelt another way

parts.note: a curb is a type of bit for a horse

explanation.surface: Sounding a little on the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: A curb bit is a horse's bit with a chain; the kerb, British spelling, is the edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerb is the edging line between pavement and road, a literal borderline.

clue.text: Stuffing things in cab, wine's overturned; Mary's gutted

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so the wine word is read backwards
gutted means having its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Packing things into a taxi: the wine has tipped over and Mary is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, but here strips Mary's middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermy is the craft of stuffing and mounting dead animals.
